new_entities.name: High-dose cocoa flavanols
new_entities.description: High-flavanol cocoa or cocoa extract interventions typically delivering several hundred milligrams of flavanols per day.

new_entities.name: Cognitive function in older adults
new_entities.description: Memory, executive function, attention, and related cognitive performance in middle-aged and older adults.

edges.effect_quant: A 2022 meta-analysis of dietary flavonoids found a significant subgroup benefit for cocoa interventions on cognition (g 0.224, p = 0.036), with stronger signals in middle-aged and older adults from chronic studies.
edges.population: middle-aged and older adults without overt dementia, sometimes with lower baseline diet quality or subjective memory concerns
edges.mechanism: Cocoa flavanols are usually framed as endothelial and neurovascular modulators that may improve cerebral blood flow and support hippocampal function. The human data fit that story only partially: benefits appear more likely in older adults, chronic dosing, or nutritionally weaker subgroups than in universally healthy high-functioning samples.
edges.summary: High-dose cocoa flavanols probably provide modest cognitive benefit in some older adults, but the effect is uneven rather than robustly universal. The most persuasive evidence comes from subgroup-level and domain-specific gains, while several respectable trials remain neutral on broad cognitive batteries.
edges.caveats: This edge is sensitive to baseline health, diet quality, dose, and the specific cognitive task used. A small average benefit should not be oversold as a reliable anti-aging cognitive intervention for every older adult.

evidence.citation: Lamport DJ et al 2022 Mol Nutr Food Res
evidence.notes: Dietary Flavonoids and Human Cognition: A Meta-Analysis.
